## About

The viewer styled with CSS. `css-class` adds a class to the viewer, and the
rules below use it to set the viewer's colors (plum, with pink links), draw a
line along the top of the caption band, and make the caption larger and italic.

```yaml
panzoom:
  css-class: plum-viewer
```

Only pages with that class get the rules, so the other pages of the site keep
the default viewer. A single image or code cell can add a class of its own, as
cases 2 and 4 show; it applies while that image is open.

The rules are in a raw HTML block on this page, which styles it. The same block
works in any Quarto document:

````markdown {.show-source}
```{=html}
<style>
.plum-viewer {
  --panzoom-backdrop: rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9);
  --panzoom-bg: #2d1236;
  --panzoom-fg: #f3e8f7;
  --panzoom-link: #ffb3d9;
}
.plum-viewer .panzoom-footer {
  border-top: 4px solid #d58cf0;
}
.plum-viewer .panzoom-caption {
  font-size: 1.15rem;
  font-style: italic;
}
.sea-viewer {
  --panzoom-backdrop: rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9);
  --panzoom-bg: #0f3640;
  --panzoom-fg: #e0f4f7;
  --panzoom-link: #7fe0d0;
}
.sea-viewer .panzoom-footer {
  border-top-color: #4fc3c9;
}
.sea-viewer .panzoom-caption {
  font-style: normal;
}
</style>
```
````

The same rules can also go in a stylesheet file, or in the page's header:

```yaml
format:
  html:
    css: viewer.css   # a file holding the rules above
```

```yaml
format:
  html:
    include-in-header:
      text: |
        <style>
        .plum-viewer { --panzoom-backdrop: rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9); }
        </style>
```

A theme's `.scss` file works too. Rules on the viewer's parts start with the
viewer's class, as above, so they win over the defaults. The parts are
`.panzoom-footer` (the caption band), `.panzoom-caption`,
`.panzoom-description`, `.panzoom-hint`, `.panzoom-close`, `.panzoom-prev`,
`.panzoom-next`, and `.panzoom-counter`.

For a whole site, put `css-class` (or any option) under `format: html:` in
`_quarto.yml`. A top-level `panzoom:` there is replaced, not merged, by a page's
own `panzoom:` options.

## 1. Markdown image {#c1 expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="plum-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(45, 18, 54)"}

```markdown {.show-source}
![An image with `.panzoom`. It opens with the plum viewer from the stylesheet, a line along the top of the caption band, a larger, italic caption, and this pink [link](https://quarto.org).](../../images/mv-2.jpg){.panzoom fig-alt="A white lighthouse against a blue sky"}
```

## 2. Class for one image {#c2 expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="sea-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(15, 54, 64)"}

The page's class stays on the viewer, so rules for `.sea-viewer` come after the
`.plum-viewer` ones to win over them.

```markdown {.show-source}
![An image with `.panzoom`, with a class of its own, `css-class="sea-viewer"`. It opens with the dark teal `.sea-viewer` rules and an upright caption, and this [link](https://quarto.org) is teal.](../../images/mv-3.jpg){.panzoom css-class="sea-viewer" fig-alt="A shingled gingerbread cottage with pink and green trim, behind a garden path"}
```

## 3. Code cell {#c3 expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="plum-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(60, 20, 70, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(45, 18, 54)"}

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of vapor pressure rising steeply with temperature"
#| panzoom: true
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   A code cell with `panzoom: true`. It opens with the plum viewer, as case 1
#|   does.

plot(pressure, type = "b", pch = 19)
```

## 4. Class for one cell {#c4 expect-open="panzoom" expect-class="sea-viewer" expect-overlay="rgba(10, 50, 60, 0.9)" expect-band="rgb(15, 54, 64)"}

```{r}
#| fig-alt: "Scatter plot of stopping distance against speed for 50 cars"
#| panzoom:
#|   css-class: sea-viewer
#| fig-cap: >-
#|   A code cell with `css-class: sea-viewer` under `#| panzoom:`. It opens with
#|   the same teal viewer as case 2.

plot(cars, pch = 19)
```
